title: SQL Commands: READ, SELECT, and WHERE
summary: Covers the R of CRUD in SQL: SELECT to read all or chosen columns, and WHERE to filter rows by a condition.

concepts.heading: SELECT
points: SELECT reads data. The playground's Show table action simply runs SELECT * FROM products behind the scenes.
The asterisk is a wildcard meaning every column. FROM names the table to read.
To read only some columns, list them separated by commas instead of the asterisk: SELECT name, price FROM products. The result omits the other columns (here id). The table itself is unchanged.

concepts.heading: WHERE
points: WHERE adds a search condition and limits the result to rows that satisfy it: SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = 1 returns just the row whose id is 1.
Text comparisons use single-quoted strings, e.g. WHERE Country = 'Mexico'. The same clause works with column lists in place of the asterisk.
SQL has more operators for conditions: equals, greater than, less than, BETWEEN, LIKE and others, listed in the W3Schools documentation. (Extra) Conditions can be combined with AND / OR.
SELECT with WHERE will be used constantly when working with SQL databases.

code_examples.caption: Reading data
code_examples.code:
SELECT * FROM products;                    -- every column, every row
SELECT name, price FROM products;          -- only two columns
SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = 1;       -- only matching rows
SELECT name FROM products WHERE price > 1; -- (Extra) comparison operator

pitfalls: (Extra) Using a double = sign as in JavaScript; SQL uses a single = for comparison.
(Extra) Double-quoting string values in WHERE; single quotes are the standard for string literals.

gaps_and_ideas: Combine with the other CRUD SQL lessons in one 'SQL basics' lesson. Tasks for this part: select all, select two columns, filter by id, filter with > and LIKE, filter text with single quotes.
Demo idea: a table viewer where typing a SELECT/WHERE query highlights the rows and columns it returns.
